 Midterms: Congress Turns Blue. What’s Your Next Trade? 10.4M Views · 351 Posts Moomoo MarketTrack joined discussion · Nov 20 21:03 Tech Rout Deepens, VIX Breaks Above 30
 Symbols -- -- -- Tap the related stocks on the image above to add them to your Watchlist. Market Overview Overnight futures are pointing lower again, with tech leading. $E-mini NASDAQ 100 Futures (DEC6) (NQmain.US)$ is -1.82% (-484.25 points) to 26,116.00, while $E-mini S&P 500 Futures (DEC6) (ESmain.US)$ is -0.93% (-67.25) to 7,130.00. $E-mini Dow Futures (DEC6) (YMmain.US)$ is -0.29% and $E-mini Russell 2000 Index Futures (DEC6) (RTYmain.US)$ is -0.35%, so the damage is concentrated in tech. The prior cash close was weak: $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ -2.02%, $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ -2.25%, $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ -2.19%, and $Russell 2000 Index (.RUT.US)$ -2.18%. The futures gap between $E-mini NASDAQ 100 Futures (DEC6) (NQmain.US)$ and $E-mini Dow Futures (DEC6) (YMmain.US)$ says this is an AI/semiconductor shock hitting megacap multiples, not a uniform risk-off unwind. Key Macro Indicators VIX: $CBOE Volatility S&P 500 Index (.VIX.US)$ is 30.83, up 8.40%, above 30 for the first time since late March; hedging demand is intense. WTI: $Crude Oil Futures (JAN7) (CLmain.US)$ is 82.37, nearly flat at -0.08%; oil is not adding inflation pressure. Curve: 2s10s is +28.25 bp and steepening; the 2Y fell about 8.3 bp, the 10Y about 7.9 bp. Gold: $XAU/USD (XAUUSD.CFD)$ is 3,572.29, down 1.46%; it broke below 3,600 as AI-led liquidation overwhelmed haven bids. USD: $USD (USDindex.FX)$ is 103.73, down 0.21%; the softer dollar is not cushioning commodities. Volatility up, yields down, but gold down is a liquidation signal, not a classic haven bid. Market Pressure The top-7 tech composite fell 2.68%, and premarket tech selling is staying broad. $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ -3.25%, $Microsoft (MSFT.US)$ -2.20%, $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ -2.17%, and $Apple (AAPL.US)$ +0.15%. Semis are the epicenter: $Micron Technology (MU.US)$ -5.02%, $Intel (INTC.US)$ -4.63%, $Palantir (PLTR.US)$ -3.95%. Oil is flat, so the scare is not from crude; pressure is from AI deleveraging and compression in tech valuations. The key support question is whether $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ stabilizes, because every bounce attempt has been sold. Trading Activity Option flows show rising downside protection demand. Put/call all is 0.9707 (+16.28%), index put/call is 1.2045 (+4.70%), and single-stock put/call is 0.9430 (+17.39%). $VVIX Index (.VVIX.US)$ is up 7.38% to 127.10, while $Cboe SKEW Index (.SKEW.US)$ eased 1.39% to 140.86. Index volume is above yesterday: $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 3.38B vs 3.09B, $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 8.33B vs 7.16B, $Russell 2000 Index (.RUT.US)$ 3.36B vs 3.15B. Equal-weight $Invesco Exchange Traded Fd Tr S&P 500 Equal Weight Etf (RSP.US)$ outperformed cap-weight $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ last session, but futures point to a broader fade. Buyers are paying up for puts across index and single-stock books, positioning for more downside rather than catching the knife. Rates No FOMC meeting is on this week's calendar; Thursday's jobless claims (consensus 19.7万) and core PCE on Nov 25 are the next catalysts. 2Y yield is 4.6853%, down roughly 8.3 bp; the 10Y is 4.9678%, down roughly 7.9 bp. The 2s10s spread is +28.25 bp and steepened because short-end rates fell more than long-end. This profile suggests duration buying for haven protection while inflation risks linger. The big risk is a hot core PCE print on Nov 25 reversing the steepening and adding equity pressure.
